senses.definition: A very small amount compared with what is needed or with what is already there.
senses.example: One scoop of water was a drop in the bucket compared with what the whole garden needed.

senses.definition: To leave something behind or give up trying to do it.
senses.example: We had to abandon our picnic plan when the storm arrived.

senses.definition: To officially put an end to a rule or practice.
senses.example: The Thirteenth Amendment said the country must abolish slavery.

senses.definition: Away from a place where you are expected to be.
senses.example: Lena was absent from school on Monday.

senses.definition: How far a number is from zero on a number line.
senses.example: Negative seven is seven units from zero, so its absolute value is seven.

senses.definition: To take in a liquid, heat, light, or something else.
senses.example: A cloth can absorb water from the table.

senses.definition: Made with shapes, lines, or colors without showing things exactly as they look in real life.
senses.example: The abstract picture used circles and dark lines to suggest a storm.

senses.definition: To say yes to something offered to you.
senses.example: I will accept your invitation to the book fair.

senses.definition: To agree that something is true or has happened.
senses.example: It took me a while to accept that the trip was canceled.

senses.definition: Something that happens without being planned, often causing harm or damage.
senses.example: By accident, I knocked the empty cup off the table.

senses.definition: To finish something you set out to do.
senses.example: We hoped to accomplish all three chores before lunch.

senses.definition: A place with a service or business where information about one person or group is kept.
senses.example: When I signed in to my library account, it showed the books I had borrowed.

senses.definition: A description of what happened.
senses.example: She gave her account of how the plant pot fell.

senses.definition: Correct and close to the real facts, amount, or result.
senses.example: Is the time on that clock accurate?

senses.definition: A pain that lasts for a while and may be steady.
senses.example: After our long walk, I felt an ache in my legs.

senses.definition: To hurt with a steady pain.
senses.example: My shoulders began to ache after I carried the heavy bag.

senses.definition: To reach a goal through work or effort.
senses.example: The club was proud to achieve its goal of collecting one hundred books.

senses.definition: The nut of an oak tree. An acorn has a hard shell and a little cap.
senses.example: An oak seedling grew where a jay had hidden an acorn.

senses.definition: From one side of a place or object to the other side.
senses.example: An ant walked across the sidewalk.

senses.definition: On the other side of something.
senses.example: The library is across the street from the park.

senses.definition: To do something instead of only thinking or talking about it.
senses.example: We must act now if we want to catch the bus.

senses.definition: To play a part in a story or show.
senses.example: Lian will act in the school play.

senses.definition: Something a person does.
senses.example: Holding the door was an act of kindness.

senses.definition: One of the main parts of a play.
senses.example: The first act takes place in a forest.

senses.definition: Something that a person or thing does.
senses.example: Picking up the litter was a helpful action.

senses.definition: The exciting or busy events in a story, game, or place.
senses.example: The action in our story starts when the map disappears.

senses.definition: Moving, working, or taking part in something.
senses.example: My dog likes to stay active by running in the yard.

senses.definition: Real or happening in fact.
senses.example: My guess was ten, but the actual number was twelve.

senses.definition: A feature passed down in a group of living things that helps them survive or have young in a particular place.
senses.example: A snowshoe hare’s broad feet are an adaptation for moving over snow.

senses.definition: A version of a work changed for a different audience or a different way of telling the story.
senses.example: We watched a movie adaptation of our favorite book.

senses.definition: To put another thing with what is already there.
senses.example: Please add your name to the list.

senses.definition: To put numbers together to find their total.
senses.example: If you add four and three, you get seven.

senses.definition: To say or write something more.
senses.example: I want to add one detail to my story.

senses.definition: The details that tell where a person, place, or thing can be found.
senses.example: Write the address on the front of the envelope.

senses.definition: To speak to someone or to a group.
senses.example: Our principal will address the students before the show.

senses.definition: To deal with a question or problem.
senses.example: The class made a plan to address the problem of noisy hallways.

senses.definition: To think highly of someone or something.
senses.example: I admire my cousin for keeping her promise.

senses.definition: To look at something with pleasure.
senses.example: We stopped to admire the bright red kites.

senses.definition: To say that something is true even if you wish it were not.
senses.example: I had to admit that I had forgotten my lunch.

senses.definition: To let someone enter a place.
senses.example: One ticket will admit two people to the show.

senses.definition: Earth mixed with water and sometimes plant material, then formed into bricks or walls and allowed to dry.
senses.example: The thick adobe walls blocked the heat in the afternoon.

senses.definition: To become a child’s legal parent or take an animal into your home as your own.
senses.example: My neighbors plan to adopt a dog from the shelter.

senses.definition: To begin to use an idea, habit, or way of doing something.
senses.example: Our club voted to adopt a new meeting time.

senses.definition: A person or animal that has grown up.
senses.example: The younger campers walked with an adult.

senses.definition: Grown up or made for grown-ups.
senses.example: An adult frog looks very different from a tadpole.

senses.definition: To move forward or go to a later stage.
senses.example: If your team wins today, it will advance to the next round.

senses.definition: A step toward something better or farther along.
senses.example: Adding a ramp was an advance that helped more people enter the building.

senses.definition: An exciting or unusual experience, often with surprises.
senses.example: Following the trail to the waterfall felt like an adventure.

senses.definition: A message designed to get people interested in a product, service, or idea.
senses.example: An advertisement for extra characters appeared during the game.

senses.definition: An idea someone gives you about what to do.
senses.example: My brother gave me advice about choosing a book.

senses.definition: To tell someone what you think would be a good thing to do.
senses.example: Our coach will advise us to warm up before the race.

senses.definition: To cause a change in someone or something.
senses.example: A rainy day can affect whether we play outside.

senses.definition: To have enough money, time, or other resources for something.
senses.example: I saved enough to afford the book I wanted.

senses.definition: Feeling fear or worry.
senses.example: I used to be afraid of loud thunder.

senses.definition: At a later time, after the event you just described.
senses.example: We planted the seeds and washed our hands afterward.

senses.definition: One more time, after it has already happened.
senses.example: Please read that last line again.

senses.definition: Touching or resting on something.
senses.example: The ladder leaned against the wall.

senses.definition: In opposition to someone or something.
senses.example: Our team played against the team in green.

senses.definition: In a way that breaks a rule or opposes what someone wants.
senses.example: Climbing the fence is against the park rules.

senses.definition: To think the same thing as someone else.
senses.example: I agree with Mina that the sign should be bigger.

senses.definition: To say that you will do what someone asks.
senses.example: We agree to take turns cleaning the art table.

senses.definition: Help given to a person or group.
senses.example: The rescue crew brought aid to people after the flood.

senses.definition: To help someone do something or help something happen.
senses.example: A bright sign can aid drivers in finding the turn.

senses.definition: A movable part near the outer end of an airplane wing that helps tip the plane to one side.
senses.example: Moving the ailerons changes how much each wing lifts.

senses.definition: A machine that helps take dust and other unwanted bits out of the air.
senses.example: A small air cleaner pulled air through a filter and blew it back into the room.

senses.definition: How hard the air pushes on something. It usually gets lower as you go higher above sea level.
senses.example: A barometer shows whether the air pressure is rising or falling.

senses.definition: A sound or device that warns people or calls for attention.
senses.example: My alarm rings at seven every morning.

senses.definition: Sudden fear that something is wrong.
senses.example: The loud bang caused alarm until we saw the fallen box.

senses.definition: To make someone feel suddenly worried or afraid.
senses.example: The strange sound can alarm a sleeping dog.

senses.definition: Paying close attention and ready to notice something.
senses.example: The alert goalie watched the ball.

senses.definition: A warning or notice that asks people to pay attention.
senses.example: We got a weather alert about heavy rain.

senses.definition: To warn someone or draw attention to something.
senses.example: The bell can alert the class that time is up.

senses.definition: A set of clear steps for solving a problem or doing a job.
senses.example: We followed an algorithm to find a name in the sorted list.

senses.definition: One of the versions of DNA that can occur at a particular place.
senses.example: Two siblings may inherit a different allele at the same place in their DNA.

senses.definition: Repeating the same starting sound in nearby words.
senses.example: “Busy bees buzzed” uses alliteration.

senses.definition: To let someone do something or let something happen.
senses.example: The rules allow us to bring one book to the reading corner.

senses.definition: A material containing a metal mixed with one or more other elements.
senses.example: Brass is an alloy that contains copper and zinc.

senses.definition: Very close to happening or being true.
senses.example: I was almost finished when the timer beeped.

senses.definition: Without other people or animals nearby or taking part.
senses.example: I was alone in the room when the phone rang.

senses.definition: By yourself, or without others joining or helping.
senses.example: I can finish this puzzle alone.

senses.definition: Following the length of a path, edge, or line.
senses.example: We walked along the river until we saw the bridge.

senses.definition: With someone or as part of what is happening.
senses.example: My sister asked to come along.

senses.definition: In a voice other people can hear.
senses.example: I read the first page aloud to the group.

senses.definition: The set of letters used to write one or more languages. The letters usually have an agreed order.
senses.example: We sang the letters of the English alphabet in order from A to Z.

senses.definition: The upper boundary on a mountain beyond which forests do not grow.
senses.example: Our path crossed the alpine treeline and the land ahead was open and windy.

senses.definition: Before now, or earlier than you expected.
senses.example: By the time I got outside, the bus had already left.

senses.definition: In addition to the thing just mentioned.
senses.example: Rosa plays soccer and also likes to draw.

senses.definition: Words that describe what matters about an image for someone who cannot see it.
senses.example: Alt text describes what the button with a picture of a house does.

senses.definition: Used to show a contrast between two things that are true.
senses.example: Although the room was small, we all found a place to sit.

senses.definition: The height of a place or object compared with sea level or another starting level.
senses.example: The airplane reached a higher altitude as it climbed above the clouds.

senses.definition: With everything counted together.
senses.example: How many crayons are there altogether?

senses.definition: Completely or in every way.
senses.example: The second puzzle was altogether different.

senses.definition: One of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gases move between air and blood.
senses.example: Oxygen can pass through the thin wall of an alveolus.

senses.definition: Causing great surprise or wonder.
senses.example: The boys built an amazing tower from paper cups.

senses.definition: A change or addition made to a formal document, a law, or a proposal.
senses.example: The class voted for an amendment to its rules about cleanup.

senses.definition: One of the small pieces a living body can join together to make a protein.
senses.example: A long chain can contain many copies of the same amino acid.

senses.definition: How much of something there is.
senses.example: Add a small amount of water to the paint.

senses.definition: To add up to a total or have a certain result.
senses.example: Two five-minute breaks amount to ten minutes.

senses.definition: A large round or oval performance space with rows of seats around an open middle.
senses.example: The crowd filled the seats in the amphitheater.

senses.definition: To make someone laugh or keep someone pleasantly busy.
senses.example: A silly puppet show can amuse the whole room.

senses.definition: A clock that shows the time with hands that move around a face.
senses.example: The short hand of the analog clock was between three and four.

senses.definition: From a time very long ago.
senses.example: The museum has bowls made in ancient times.

senses.definition: A strong feeling of being upset about something.
senses.example: I counted to five when I felt my anger growing.

senses.definition: To make someone angry.
senses.example: It can anger people when someone pushes to the front of the line.

senses.definition: The amount of turn or opening between two lines or directions that meet.
senses.example: The pages of the book made a wider angle when I opened it farther.

senses.definition: Making pictures or objects seem to move by showing a series of slightly different images in order.
senses.example: Her animation showed a toy elephant walking across the desk.

senses.definition: To tell people something in a way many of them can hear or see.
senses.example: The coach will announce the teams after lunch.

senses.definition: To bother someone or make them a little angry.
senses.example: The squeak might annoy you after a few minutes.

senses.definition: Happening once each year or covering one year.
senses.example: Our annual picnic happens every June.

senses.definition: A plant that usually grows, makes seeds, and finishes its life in one growing season.
senses.example: This marigold is an annual.

senses.definition: A reply to a question or a way to solve a problem.
senses.example: I wrote the answer below the math problem.

senses.definition: To give a reply or respond to someone or something.
senses.example: Can you answer this question before we start?

senses.definition: Worried about what might happen.
senses.example: I felt anxious before my first piano lesson.

senses.definition: Very eager for something to happen.
senses.example: The team was anxious to get back on the field after the rain.

senses.definition: A system of laws that separated people by race in South Africa and gave most political power to white people.
senses.example: People in South Africa and around the world organized against apartheid.

senses.definition: A home made of rooms inside a larger building.
senses.example: Our apartment is on the third floor.

senses.definition: To tell someone you are sorry for something you did or said.
senses.example: I will apologize for interrupting your story.

senses.definition: To come into sight or arrive where people can see you.
senses.example: A squirrel may appear when the yard is quiet.

senses.definition: To seem a certain way.
senses.example: The two jars appear to be the same size.

senses.definition: A round fruit with firm flesh and a thin skin.
senses.example: I added slices of apple to my lunch.

senses.definition: To formally ask for something, such as a job or a place in a program.
senses.example: I want to apply for a spot in the summer camp.

senses.definition: To put something onto a surface.
senses.example: We used a brush to apply paint to the sign.

senses.definition: To be true or useful in a particular case.
senses.example: The same rules apply to everyone in the game.

senses.definition: A planned time to meet someone or do something with them.
senses.example: We have an appointment to get our dog checked.

senses.definition: To recognize and value what someone has done or what something gives you.
senses.example: I appreciate your help with the heavy boxes.

senses.definition: To say yes to a plan or request.
senses.example: The teacher has to approve our idea for the class party.

senses.definition: To think that something is right or good.
senses.example: My grandparents approve of our plan to share the chores.

senses.definition: A channel or pipe built to carry water from one place to another, sometimes across a bridge.
senses.example: The ancient aqueduct carried water to people living in the city.

senses.definition: A layer of material under the ground that holds water and lets enough move through to supply a well or spring.
senses.example: The well reached an aquifer with water between grains of sand.

senses.definition: A curved structure that spans an opening and helps hold up what is above it.
senses.example: The stone arch carried the weight of the wall over the doorway.

senses.definition: A scientist who studies the people of the past through things they left behind, such as tools, buildings, or pieces of pottery.
senses.example: The archaeologist drew a map of where each piece of pottery was found.

senses.definition: A group or chain of islands. It can also mean the area of water that holds them.
senses.example: We took a boat between two islands in the archipelago.

senses.definition: A collection of records saved so people can consult them in the future, or the place that keeps them.
senses.example: The town archive has photographs of the old train station.

senses.definition: To save material in a collection for future use.
senses.example: We will archive the school’s old yearbooks instead of throwing them away.

senses.definition: Land in the far north where the weather is cold and mostly low plants can grow.
senses.example: A thin layer of soil thawed in summer on the arctic tundra.

senses.definition: The amount of flat space inside a shape.
senses.example: The area of the tiled floor is 24 square meters.

senses.definition: A particular part of a place.
senses.example: We ate in a shaded area of the park.

senses.definition: To disagree with someone, especially while speaking strongly.
senses.example: We sometimes argue about whose turn it is.

senses.definition: To give reasons for thinking something is true or right.
senses.example: The class will argue for more time to read.

senses.definition: An agreement by people or countries fighting a war to stop the fighting.
senses.example: The armistice took effect later on the same morning.

senses.definition: To put things in an order or pattern.
senses.example: Please arrange the books from shortest to tallest.

senses.definition: To make plans for something to happen.
senses.example: Our teacher will arrange a visit to the museum.

senses.definition: A group arranged in rows and columns or another orderly pattern.
senses.example: An array of three rows with four seeds in each row has twelve seeds.

senses.definition: To reach the place you are going to.
senses.example: What time will the bus arrive at the library?

senses.definition: A tube that carries blood away from the heart.
senses.example: Blood leaves the heart in an artery.

senses.definition: Feeling bad or embarrassed about something you did.
senses.example: I felt ashamed after laughing at my friend’s mistake.

senses.definition: To one side or away from the usual or main place.
senses.example: I stepped aside so the group could pass.

senses.definition: A short comment said to one person or an audience, separate from the main talk.
senses.example: In an aside to the audience, the actor explained where the key was hidden.

senses.definition: To use a question to get information or request something.
senses.example: Ask your partner which color they want.

senses.definition: To invite someone to do something.
senses.example: I will ask Jae to join our game.

senses.definition: Sleeping.
senses.example: The kitten was asleep inside its basket.

senses.definition: To help someone do something.
senses.example: Two parents will assist with the science fair.

senses.definition: A rule that says changing which numbers you group first in addition or multiplication leaves the answer the same.
senses.example: The associative property lets us add the last two numbers in six plus seven plus three first.

senses.definition: To believe something is true without knowing for sure.
senses.example: I assumed the box was empty until I heard it rattle.

senses.definition: A small, mostly rocky object that circles the Sun. Many of them travel between Mars and Jupiter.
senses.example: A spacecraft can take close-up pictures of an asteroid.

senses.definition: With just a quick look.
senses.example: I could tell at a glance which jar held more marbles.

senses.definition: At the smallest amount mentioned, or more.
senses.example: For this project, each robot needs at least two wheels.

senses.definition: At the largest amount mentioned, or less.
senses.example: The bookcase can hold at most three more books on that shelf.

senses.definition: The layer of gases held around a planet, moon, or star by gravity.
senses.example: Clouds form in Earth’s atmosphere.

senses.definition: The feeling that a place or event gives the people there.
senses.example: Soft music gave the room a calm atmosphere.

senses.definition: A tiny piece of matter that is still one particular chemical element. Gold is made of gold atoms, for example.
senses.example: An atom of oxygen is so small you cannot see it with your eyes.

senses.definition: To join or fasten one thing to another.
senses.example: We used a clip to attach the note to the bag.

senses.definition: A try at doing something.
senses.example: On my third attempt, the paper airplane reached the door.

senses.definition: To try to do something.
senses.example: I will attempt the harder puzzle when I have more time.

senses.definition: To be at an event or go regularly to a place such as school.
senses.example: We plan to attend the concert on Friday.

senses.definition: The act of looking, listening, or thinking closely about something.
senses.example: The little bird caught my attention when it landed on the fence.

senses.definition: The people who watch, read, or listen to a performance, story, or message.
senses.example: The audience clapped when the play ended.

senses.definition: A glow in a planet’s upper atmosphere caused by particles giving energy to a gas there.
senses.example: An aurora looked like a green curtain over the dark hills.

senses.definition: A person who writes a book, story, or other work.
senses.example: The author chose a dog as the main character.

senses.definition: The season between summer and winter.
senses.example: In autumn, many trees lose their leaves.

senses.definition: Ready to be used, taken, or talked to.
senses.example: Three computers are available at the library today.

senses.definition: A number found by adding several amounts and dividing by how many amounts there are.
senses.example: The average of two and six is four.

senses.definition: Usual or close to what you would expect.
senses.example: On an average day, the walk takes about ten minutes.

senses.definition: To stay away from someone or something, or keep something from happening.
senses.example: We took the dry path to avoid the mud.

senses.definition: Not sleeping.
senses.example: I was awake before my alarm rang.

senses.definition: To wake up or cause someone to wake up.
senses.example: The first campers awoke at sunrise.
